mappings.note: Convert 37 C to Fahrenheit. A physical quantity expressed on a second scale, LO-72; no phenomenon is explained, so not LO-71.
Fill the blanks: temperature determines hotness, a clinical thermometer cannot read ice-cold water, the unit is degree Celsius. Quantity, instrument range and unit, all LO-72.
The laboratory thermometer's range is -10 C to 110 C. The span an instrument can measure, LO-72.
Which of four students measured the water temperature correctly. Judging the conduct of an investigation -- bulb immersed, not touching the vessel, eye level -- LO-69.
Colour the liquid column on drawn thermometers to show given temperatures. Producing a labelled diagram of an instrument, LO-73.
Predict, then conduct the activity and write your observations. The predict-do-record cycle, LO-69.
Watch the liquid column rise and report the reading. Observation during a conducted activity, LO-69.
Analyse ten days of maximum and minimum air temperature. LO-69 for interpreting a recorded data set, LO-72 because the data are temperature measurements.
Normal healthy body temperature is 37.0 C. A standard value of a physical quantity, LO-72. The printed answer belongs to a different item -- it carries Activity 7.2's text instead of the option.
Read off the lowest and highest values an instrument can show and state its range. Instrument range, LO-72.
Work out the least count by counting divisions between the big marks. The resolution of a measuring instrument, LO-72.
Name the thermometer type, read its value, and give its least count. Reading a measuring instrument, LO-72.
Why a laboratory thermometer cannot serve for body temperature. The answer contrasts the two instruments on range and the locking constriction -- a differentiation by structure and function, LO-67.
Read Vaishnavi's fever chart for the peak value, when it occurred and when it normalised. Interpreting recorded observations over time, LO-69. The stem opens with a stray '6 C' fragment.
Which of three thermometers can read 22.5 C, and why. Choosing an instrument by range and least count, LO-72.
Read 27.5 C from a column halfway between marks on a 0.5 C scale. A measurement taken from an instrument, LO-72.
Fifty divisions across 100 C gives 2 C per division. Least count computed, LO-72.
DRAW the 10 C to 20 C portion of a scale whose smallest division is 0.5 C. Producing a labelled diagram, LO-73. The printed answer is the next item's stem.
Komal's '101 degrees' must be Fahrenheit, since 101 C is impossible for a body. Reading an everyday statement against what the scales mean, LO-75.
Temperature is a reliable measure of hotness or coldness. Defines the physical quantity, LO-72.
Phiban used a thermometer to confirm the fever. An instrument used in a household situation, LO-75; this is narrative recall rather than a measuring task.
Why touch misleads -- the sensation depends on the hand's previous exposure. The item asks for the CAUSE of an unreliable judgement, LO-70.
A thermometer is a device that measures temperature. The measuring instrument named, LO-72.
The clinical thermometer is used for body temperature. Matching instrument to quantity, LO-72.
Digital thermometers avoid mercury poisoning and read more easily. A practical judgement about which instrument to use at home, LO-75.
The Celsius unit is the degree Celsius. The unit of a physical quantity, LO-72.
Normal body temperature is 37.0 C. A standard value of the quantity, LO-72.
The key difference in USE between clinical and laboratory thermometers. An explicit differentiation of two instruments by function, LO-67.
Wash the tip with soap and water before and after use. A handling rule for a household instrument, LO-75.
Why a healthy person may differ from 37.0 C -- age, time of day, activity. The item asks for causes of the variation, LO-70.
37.0 C equals 98.6 F. A quantity expressed on a second scale, LO-72.
The SI unit of temperature is the kelvin. LO-72 is 'express them in SI units' exactly, and this is the chapter's clearest instance.
Why a clinical thermometer cannot read boiling water or ice -- its range excludes them. Instrument range against the quantity to be measured, LO-72.
The red liquid in a laboratory thermometer is dyed alcohol. Identifying the material inside the instrument, LO-66.
Ten divisions across 10 C gives 1 C each. Least count computed, LO-72.
Why the reading must be taken with the bulb still immersed. Correct conduct of the investigation, LO-69.
Temperature stays constant while water boils or ice melts. Explaining what happens during a phase change, LO-71.
The constriction that lets a clinical thermometer hold its reading, which a laboratory one lacks. A differentiation by structure, LO-67. Option (D) is truncated with its tail in the stem.
Which is NOT a precaution -- letting the bulb touch the beaker bottom. Correct conduct of the investigation, LO-69.
Assertion-reason: touch is unreliable BECAUSE the sensation depends on previous exposure. The causal clause is what is marked, LO-70.

Which statements about the SI unit, the Fahrenheit unit and the kelvin's missing degree sign are correct. Units and their conventions, LO-72. The stem retains only the last of the three numbered statements.
Non-contact screening thermometers are infrared thermometers. A measuring technology met in public life, LO-75; the frame has no LO for radiation-based instruments.
Why the tip is washed -- to stop infection spreading between users. Hygiene in shared use of an instrument, LO-75.
The laboratory thermometer's usual range. Instrument range, LO-72.
An armpit reading runs about 0.5 C below core temperature. A systematic offset in a measurement, LO-72.
The kelvin is written without the degree sign. A unit-writing convention, LO-72.
Which action to AVOID -- letting the bulb touch the container. Correct conduct of the measurement, LO-69.
What the maximum air temperature in a weather report means. Reading a measurement met in daily life, LO-75.

Assertion-reason: mercury thermometers are replaced because mercury is toxic and hazardous when broken. The reason is an environmental and safety hazard, which is LO-76's register, not a measurement point.

Which statements about a digital clinical thermometer hold -- battery operated, needs body contact, and must NOT be held by the tip. Safe handling in practice, LO-75. Only one of the three numbered statements survives in the stem.
Choose the laboratory thermometer for melting ice because its range reaches 0 C. Selecting an instrument by range, LO-72.
Absolute zero is 0 kelvin, about -273.15 C. The lower bound of the quantity on the SI scale, LO-72.
Why the eye must be level with the liquid column -- parallax error. Correct conduct of the reading, LO-69.
The three scales are named after the scientists who devised them. A history-of-science fact with no LO to hold it; cited at CG-SCI1, which covers the nature of scientific knowledge.
What Activity 7.1's tap water feels like to each hand. Reporting the result of the conducted activity, LO-69, where item 22 asked for its cause and got LO-70.
Fahrenheit is no longer the scientific scale. Choice of unit system for a quantity, LO-72.
Blood type is NOT among the factors affecting body temperature. Tests which causes genuinely influence the quantity, LO-70.
Twenty degrees across ten divisions gives 2 C each. Least count computed, LO-72.
Temperature is the reliable measure of hotness or coldness. Defining the physical quantity, LO-72.
The device that measures temperature is the thermometer. Naming the measuring instrument, LO-72.
